Rashi on Megillah 13a:10:1.hebrew: בין ההדסים אשר במצולה - בין הצדיקים שגלו לבבל, ובשכינה משתעי קרא:
Rashi on Megillah 13a:10:1.english: Among the myrtles that were in the deep - Among the righteous who were exiled to Babylonia, and the verse speaks of the Divine Presence [Shekhinah].

Rashi on Megillah 13a:12:1.english: Istahar - Moon; [she was] as beautiful as the moon:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:12:2.english: She was greenish - like this myrtle:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:12:3.hebrew: אלא חוט של חסד משוך עליה - מאת הקב"ה, לכך נראית יפה לאומות ולאחשורוש:
Rashi on Megillah 13a:12:3.english: Rather, a thread of grace was drawn upon her - From the Holy One, blessed be He; therefore, she appeared beautiful to the nations and to Ahasuerus.

Rashi on Megillah 13a:13:1.hebrew: ובמות אביה ואמה תו ל"ל - מאחר דכתיב "כי אין לה אב ואם"? אלא ללמדנו שאפי' יום אחד לא היה לה אב ואם:
Rashi on Megillah 13a:13:1.english: And when her father and mother were dead, why do I further need [this] - since it is [already] written, "For she had neither father nor mother"? Rather, [it comes] to teach us that not even [for] one day did she have a father and mother:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:13:2.english: When her mother became pregnant [with her], her father died - It follows that she did not have a father from the moment [he] was fit to be called a father:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:13:3.english: And when she gave birth to her, her mother died - and she [her mother] was not fit to be called "mother":

Rashi on Megillah 13a:14:1.english: But the poor man had nothing - The verse is speaking about Uriah:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:15:1.hebrew: שהיתה מונה בהן ימי שבת - שהיתה משרתת לה אחת באחד בשבת, ואחת בשני בשבת, ואחת בשלישי בשבת, וכן כולן; וכשהגיע יום שפחה של שבת, יודעת שהיום שבת:
Rashi on Megillah 13a:15:1.english: That she would count the days of the week by them - For one [maidservant] would serve her on the first [day] of the week, and one on the second [day] of the week, and one on the third [day] of the week, and so [with] all of them; and when the day of the maidservant of Shabbat arrived, she knew that it was Shabbat:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:16:1.hebrew: כתלי דחזירי - בקונ"וש שמינים, ומתוך אונסה לא נענשה:
Rashi on Megillah 13a:16:1.english: Pig hinds - Fatty bacons [Old French], and because she was compelled, she was not punished:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:17:1.hebrew: ויהי המלצר נושא את פת בגם ויין משתיהם וגו' - וכתיב בההוא ענינא: "ולמקצת ימים עשרה נראה מראיהם טוב ובריאי בשר" וגו':
Rashi on Megillah 13a:17:1.english: So the steward took away their food and the wine that they should drink, etc. - And it is written in that passage: "And at the end of ten days, their appearance looked better and healthier in flesh," etc.:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:18:1.hebrew: אנפקינון שמן זית שלא הביא שליש - גבי מנחות תנן: "אין מביאין אנפקינון, ואם הביא פסול", ועלה קאי ר' יהודה ואמר מהו אנפקינון:
Rashi on Megillah 13a:18:1.english: Anpakinon [is] the oil of olives that have not reached one-third [of their growth] - Regarding meal-offerings, we learned [in a Mishnah]: "We do not bring anpakinon, and if one brought [it], it is disqualified," and Rabbi Yehudah is referring to that [Mishnah] and stating what anpakinon is.

Rashi on Megillah 13a:19:1.english: From the disgrace of that wicked man - This is his disgrace, that he cohabits with women and sends them away:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:20:1.hebrew: שהגוף נהנה מן הגוף - מפני הצינה, והעיד לך הכתוב שהיו מתכונין מן השמים לחבבה על בעלה:
Rashi on Megillah 13a:20:1.english: That the body derives pleasure from [another] body - because of the cold, and Scripture testifies to you that from Heaven they intended to endear her to her husband:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:21:1.hebrew: ביקש לטעום כו' - לכך נאמר "מכל הנשים" ו"מכל הבתולות":
Rashi on Megillah 13a:21:1.english: [If] he wanted to taste, etc. - That is why it is stated, "more than all the women" and "more than all the virgins."

Rashi on Megillah 13a:22:1.hebrew: עבד משתיא כו' - חוזר לכמה ענינים לפייסה שתגלה לו מולדתה, ולא הועיל; וסמוך לה להאי קרא: "ובהקבץ בתולות שנית וגו'", "אין אסתר מגדת מולדתה ואת עמה וגו'". "עבד משתיא" — סעודה לכבודה, מה שלא עשה בשאר נשים:
Rashi on Megillah 13a:22:1.english: He made a feast, etc. - He [Ahasuerus] tried various ways to appease her so that she would reveal her birthplace to him, but it did not avail; and adjacent to this verse [is written]: "And when the virgins were gathered together the second time, etc." [Esther 2:19], "Esther had not yet made known her kindred nor her people, etc." [Esther 2:20]. "He made a feast" — [meaning] a banquet in her honor, which he did not do for the other women:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:22:2.hebrew: דלי כרגא - אמר: "בשביל אסתר אני מניח לכם מכסי גולגולתכם", היינו "והנחה למדינות עשה":
Rashi on Megillah 13a:22:2.english: He lowered the tax - [The king] said, "For Esther's sake, I am waiving your head taxes for you" — this is [what is meant by], "and he granted a remission to the provinces" [Esther 2:18]:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:22:3.hebrew: שדר פרדישני - דורונות לשרים בשמה, והיינו דכתיב "ויתן משאת כיד המלך":
Rashi on Megillah 13a:22:3.english: He sent pardishenei - [meaning] gifts to the ministers in her name, and this is what is written: "and he gave gifts according to the bounty of the king" [Esther 2:18]:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:2:1.hebrew: איתי גוברין יהודאין כו' - וסיפיה דקרא: "לאלהך לא פלחין":
Rashi on Megillah 13a:2:1.english: There are certain Jews [Yehuda’in], etc. - And the end of the verse [states]: "They do not serve your gods."

Rashi on Megillah 13a:3:1.hebrew: כל דבריך אחד הן - כנגד הספר היה אומר: כל דבריך, דברי הימים, אחת הן — הרבה שמות אתה מזכיר, פלוני ופלוני, וכולן אדם אחד הן:
Rashi on Megillah 13a:3:1.english: All of your words are one - He was addressing the book: "All of your words, [O] Chronicles, are one — you mention many names, so-and-so and so-and-so, and they are all one person."

Rashi on Megillah 13a:3:2.hebrew: ואנו יודעין לדורשן - ואע"פ שסתמת אותן, אנו נותנין את לבינו עד שאנו יודעין לדורשן. משום דאמרינן לעיל "כל הכופר בע"ז נקרא יהודי", נקט לה הכא:
Rashi on Megillah 13a:3:2.english: And we know how to expound them - And even though you [the book of Chronicles] have obscured them, we apply our minds until we know how to expound them. Because we said above, "Anyone who repudiates idolatry is called a Jew [Yehudi]," [the Gemara] cites this [passage] here:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:3:3.hebrew: ואשתו היהודיה וגו' - והלא בתיה שמה, דהא כתיב בסופיה: "ואלה בני בתיה":
Rashi on Megillah 13a:3:3.english: And his wife HaYehudiyya, etc. - Was her name not Bithiah, for it is written at the end [of the verse]: "And these are the sons of Bithiah"?

Rashi on Megillah 13a:4:1.english: To wash - to immerse (an expression of) conversion:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:8:1.english: Wasn’t his name Caleb? - For the verse is speaking about Caleb:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:8:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: "וישא בתיה שמרדה בגילולי בית אביה" - ולכך נשתנה שמה בליקוחין הללו:
Rashi on Megillah 13a:8:2.english: This is how we read [the text]: “and marry Bithiah, who rebelled against the idols of her father’s home” - And therefore her name was changed [to Bithiah] in this marriage:

Rashi on Megillah 13a:9:1.hebrew: שגלה מעצמו - מדלא כתיב "אשר היה מן הגולה אשר הגלתה", וכתיב "אשר הגלה עם הגולה", משמע שלא היה כשאר ישראל שגלו על כרחן, והוא גלה מעצמו, כמו שעשה ירמיהו שגלה מעצמו, עד שאמר לו הקב"ה לחזור:
Rashi on Megillah 13a:9:1.english: That he went into exile on his own - Since it is not written "who was of the exile that had been exiled," and [instead] it is written "who had been exiled with the exile," it implies that he was not like the rest of Israel who were exiled against their will; rather, he went into exile on his own, just as Jeremiah did, who went into exile on his own until the Holy One, blessed be He, told him to return:

Tosafot on Megillah 13a:16:1.hebrew: קדלי דחזירי - וח"ו, היא לא היתה אוכלת:
Tosafot on Megillah 13a:16:1.english: Necks of pigs - And Heaven forbid, she did not eat [them]:

Tosafot on Megillah 13a:2:1.hebrew: כל הכופר בע"ז נקרא יהודי שנאמר איתי גוברין יהודאין - על שם יהודי, שהרי אמר בחלק (סנהדרין דף צג:) דלא הוו משבט יהודה:
Tosafot on Megillah 13a:2:1.english: Anyone who repudiates idolatry is called Yehudi, as it is stated: “There are certain Yehuda’in” - [They were called so] on account of [the designation] Yehudi, for [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] Ḥelek (Sanhedrin 93b) that they were not from the tribe of Judah:

Tosafot on Megillah 13a:9:1.english: Who had been exiled ... that he went into exile on his own - And he expounds it from [the fact] that it is not written הוגלה [with a vav]:
